newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall below 2,600 on poll rumours.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall below 2,600 on poll rumours.

text.p: French stocks plunged below 2,600 points at midday on Wednesday on talk that privately commissioned polls showed the opposition Socialists in the lead going into Sunday's parliamentary election, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 118 points, or 4.42 percent, at 2,561.46 at 1040 GMT with all shares in the index showing declines.
One trader said the market was being bombarded by rumours and was feeling fragile with more private polls due on Thursday.
"We're hearing everything. You can't imagine," he said.
Brokers said the talk was that privately commissioned polls -- which may not be divulged publicly under French law -- showed the left ahead in percentage terms and in legislative seats.
They said President Jacques Chirac's efforts to boost the ruling centre-right RPR-UDF coalition after its poor performance in the first round of polling on Sunday did not seem convincing.
